reference.title: Alternate Lying Floor Leg Raise
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the leg rises, in as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 1.3 s down per leg

prescription.tempo: About 1 s up, short pause, 1.5 s down
prescription.progression: Slower lowering, then both legs hovering (alternate leg raise), then ankle weights

cues.text: Lie flat, arms by your sides palms down, both legs straight on the mat.
Brace and lift the right leg straight up toward vertical; the left leg stays on the mat.
Lower it slowly back to the mat without letting the low back arch.
Same with the left leg; the right leg rests.
Both legs down, breathe, and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching as the leg lowers
mistakes.fix: Brace first and keep the ribs down; shorten the range if the back lifts.
Keep the knee long; lift only as high as the hamstrings allow.
Hands rest lightly; the abdominals hold the pelvis.
Lower under control, slower than the lift.

kinematics.norm: Up to about vertical (75-90 degrees), limited by hamstring length (clinical opinion)
From 0 to about 80-90 degrees on the lifting side (clinical opinion)
Stays on the mat; a single straight-leg raise loads the spine less than a double one (McGill 1998)
Pelvis stays still on the mat (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up and 1.5 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual 976, Alternate Lying Floor Leg Raise, video (movement reference)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)
Andersson, Nilsson, Ma and Thorstensson 1997, abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises (Eur J Appl Physiol 75:115-123; PMID 9118976)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low-back pain: bend the resting knee with the foot flat; it keeps the pelvis level.
Pregnancy and postpartum (diastasis recti): get individual guidance before straight-leg work.
modify: Bend the resting knee, foot flat.
progressions: Alternate leg raise with both legs hovering.

muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris lift the right leg; leg raises gave high psoas activity in McGill's comparison (McGill 1998).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris lift the left leg in its turn.
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and transversus hold the pelvis still against the pull of the lifting leg (Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Rectus femoris helps flex the hip and keeps the knee straight.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Rectus femoris helps flex the hip and keeps the knee straight.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Help flex the hip near the floor and keep the leg in line.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Help flex the hip near the floor and keep the leg in line.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the pelvis rotating toward the lifting leg.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the pelvis rotating toward the lifting leg.

phases.label: Raise and lower the left leg
